label: Inverse Kinematics
notes: Across printed pages 219 to 244 the chapter inverts the forward map: given a desired end-effector pose, recover joint values that achieve it. We frame the whole topic as root finding on a geometric residual, motivating both closed-form geometric solutions and iterative numerical schemes built from the Jacobian.

label: The Inverse Problem
notes: Forward kinematics sends joint vectors to a pose; inversion seeks a preimage of a target. Because the map is nonlinear and periodic, a reachable target may admit several joint solutions, none, or one hard to approach. The practical question is local: which tangent direction in joint space reduces the current pose error.

label: Analytic IK: Planar 2R Arm
notes: For special geometries we solve in closed form. A planar two-link arm reaches a point by the law of cosines, which fixes the elbow angle up to sign. The wrapped first angle then aligns the shoulder. This gives an exact algebraic recipe rather than an iterative search over configurations.

label: Elbow-Up and Elbow-Down
notes: The cosine law leaves the elbow sign free, so one reachable target yields two postures: elbow-up and elbow-down. They share an endpoint yet occupy different regions of configuration space. This branch multiplicity is generic; analytic solvers enumerate branches while numerical solvers land on whichever basin the initial guess selects.

label: Newton-Raphson on Pose Error
notes: When no closed form exists we linearize. Reading the configuration error as a body twist from the matrix logarithm of T inverse times the target, Newton-Raphson repeatedly corrects the joint vector using the body Jacobian. Each step trusts the first-order model of the forward map near the current configuration.

label: The Body Twist Error
notes: The residual must match the Jacobian convention. We express the error as a body twist whose matrix log captures both rotation and translation discrepancy between current and target frames in a single six-vector. Mixing body, space, and coordinate errors can look plausible while pushing the iteration in the wrong direction.

label: The Iteration Step
notes: The core update multiplies the Jacobian pseudoinverse by the body twist and adds it to the joints. When the Jacobian is square and full rank this is the exact Newton step; otherwise the pseudoinverse selects the least-norm joint update. Convergence is quadratic near a solution but only inside a basin around the guess.

label: The Pseudoinverse
notes: The Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse handles non-square and rank-deficient Jacobians. For redundant arms it returns the minimum-norm joint velocity achieving the task twist; for overdetermined tasks it returns the least-squares fit. It is the workhorse that turns a singular or rectangular linear system into a well-defined joint correction.

label: Damping Near Singularity
notes: Near a singularity the Jacobian loses rank and the raw pseudoinverse demands enormous joint motion for tiny task corrections. Damped least squares adds a regularizer, trading exact local correction for bounded, robust steps. The notebook sweep confirms stronger damping shrinks the peak update while usually costing extra iterations to reach tolerance.

label: Redundancy and Null Space
notes: A redundant arm has more joints than task dimensions, so its Jacobian has a nontrivial null space. Adding any null-space velocity changes posture without altering first-order end-effector motion. This freedom lets secondary objectives, like avoiding joint limits or obstacles, ride along with the primary task through the projector I minus J-dagger J.

label: Convergence Basins
notes: Inverse kinematics is local and branch dependent. The notebook drives three seeds toward one target: a straight-arm singular seed plus elbow-up and elbow-down guesses. All reach the target to tolerance, yet the two elbow branches end far apart in joint space, confirming that small task residual does not identify a unique configuration.

label: Recap and Pitfalls
notes: We recap: analytic IK enumerates branches for special geometries; Newton-Raphson with the body Jacobian inverts general poses; the pseudoinverse and damping handle redundancy and singularity; null-space motion resolves extra freedom. Pitfalls include wrong-branch convergence, large motion near singularities, and residual conventions that quietly mismatch the Jacobian.
